feature: See-through things are the shade a browser draws
summary: In Next, shadows, faded layers and soft edges now mix with what is under them the way a browser, Figma and the exported SVG do, so the icon you approve is the icon you hand over. A 55% black shadow over white is 191 on the canvas and 190 in the file, where it used to be 192 against 134.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default.

try.do: Open any drawing that has a soft shadow or a layer below 100% opacity on a white page, and look at how deep the shadow reads now.
Draw a rectangle on a white page, add a Shadow in Effects, and set its Opacity to 55%.
Choose File, Export, save it as SVG, and open the file in Safari beside the canvas.
Set the shadow's colour to a deep navy, export again, and compare the colour in the browser.
Open the settings pane screenshot, run Separate into Layers, and drag the first card away from where it was.
Open Experiments, turn off "See-through things are the shade a browser draws", then close and reopen the drawing to compare it with the lighter mix.

evaluate: Does the exported shadow in the browser look the same shade as the one on the canvas?
Do your existing drawings still look right with deeper shadows, or does one now look too heavy?
Does a navy shadow read as navy, rather than grey-blue?
Does a separated card's shadow still match the screenshot it came off, with no grey halo left behind?
rough: Every see-through thing in an existing drawing is deeper in Next than it was. A shadow you nudged by eye until it looked right may now look heavier than you meant.
Current is left exactly as it was, so Current's canvas and its exported SVG still disagree on shadow shade.
In Current a coloured shadow still comes out washed toward grey. Next fixes that: the colour was being faded by its own opacity twice.
Blurs and blend modes now mix in the same space as the web too, so a blur's soft edge reads a little darker than before.
Flipping the switch reaches an open canvas only on its next redraw (the next edit), so the steps say to reopen the drawing.
There is no mock for this: the side-by-side is the decision's own pair of pictures, and the second shot here is the real window.
